blueprints.docs_preview:
# CLI Rust Architecture Guide — Unified Track

This is the unified documentation track combining the best patterns from [ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep) (performance, builder, cross-platform) and [agent-cli-framework](https://github.com/paperfoot/agent-cli-framework) (JSON envelope, exit contracts, agent discoverability, config). Files from these two source sets were selected to eliminate contradictions — use this track for implementation, not the source docs directly.

For a complete working example implementing every pattern, see `agent-cli-framework/example/` in this repository.

## Architecture & setup

- **module-layout.md** — organize src/ into focused modules
- **crate-workspace.md** — split into workspace crates (for larger projects)
- **builder-pattern.md** — Builder pattern for configurable components
- **push-model-pipeline.md** — trait-based processing pipeline

## CLI interface

- **clap-derive-commands.md** — Clap derive for Cli + Commands + args
- **dual-output-format.md** — auto-detect TTY vs pipe for JSON/human output
- **json-envelope.md** — standard JSON envelope for all responses
- **non-interactive-design.md** — no prompts, --confirm flag, exit on missing auth

# desktop-rust-gpui Blueprint

Runnable reference for a GPUI desktop app whose business core is a separate, platform-independent Rust artefact — zero gpui in core, actor/repository + REST/SSE behind a thin rsx UI, consumer-driven pact contracts verified against a local stub. The v2 example (change-on-top) assembles a **dock app shell** (`DockArea`: left sidebar, center tabview, collapsed bottom/right docks) and a **Configuration modal built from the stock gpui-component `Settings` shell** — schema-driven typed fields per config key (`GET /configs/{key}/schema`), live-save per field over PUT, built-in Reset All.

## Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| Language | Rust 1.95.0 (`rust-toolchain.toml` per crate), edition 2024, macOS only (A2) |
| UI framework | GPUI 0.2.2 (`default-features=false`, `runtime_shaders`) |
| UI components | gpui-component 0.5.1 (`default-features=false`) |
| rsx macro | gpui-rsx **vendored fork** @ commit `b8d3d49` (`no_id` + `key`→`SharedString` fixes — no crates.io publish, B1) |
| Core | tokio (`rt-multi-thread`, `macros`, `sync`), reqwest (`json`, `streaming`), serde/serde_json, chrono |
| Stub | axum 0.8, tokio, tokio-stream, serde_json |
| Contract testing | `pact_consumer` 1.4.x (core dev-dep) · `pact_verifier` 1.4.x (stub dev-dep) |
| UI extras | rust-i18n 3, uuid (v4 instance ids), tokio (`sync` only — no runtime), chrono, serde_json, image + ab_glyph (storybook screenshot fallback) |

## Mandatory Workflow

This repository uses architecture-first development. Before coding, load the relevant docs from `docs/arch` and follow them strictly.

1. Identify the task type (domain change, API, persistence, projection, cross-context flow, tests).
2. Read matching doc files listed below.
3. Implement only through existing architectural patterns.
4. Add or update tests in the same context package.
5. Verify ArchUnit constraints remain valid.

If a task touches multiple contexts, read `context-boundaries.md` and `adapter-mediator.md` first.

### Document Map

| File | What it covers |
|------|----------------|
| `code-structure.md` | Package layout, naming conventions, module organization |
| `ports.md` | Primary/secondary ports and mediator-based cross-context contracts |
| `domain-model.md` | Aggregates, value objects, domain events, invariant placement |
| `policy.md` | Business calculations and decision policies |

blueprints.docs_preview:
# Documentation Index

Universal instructions for building a conforming Rust microservice (axum + sqlx, bounded contexts, ports & adapters, DDD, semantic errors, Keycloak, OTel, k8s). Each entry is imperative: read the doc when doing that task. Code examples use the tenant-scoped settings store as the recurring worked example.

## Architecture & structure

**code-structure.md** — read when scaffolding a new slice/module or deciding where a file goes (the generalized per-context flat, business-named layout: `model.rs`, `settings.rs`, `settings_repository.rs`, `pg_settings.rs`, `error.rs`, `rest.rs`).

**vertical-slices.md** — read when converting a layered codebase into slices, or when explaining the C2 layered → sliced transform (the settings bounded context as the worked example).

**bounded-contexts.md** — read when deciding a context's boundary, its public surface, or how two contexts interact (only via ports/events, never direct imports or cross-DB).

**ports-and-adapters.md** — read when defining a port (service/repository trait), building an adapter, or wiring the composition root (generic ports with native `async fn`, static dispatch — no `Arc<dyn …>`, no `#[async_trait]`).

**ddd-building-blocks.md** — read when modeling an aggregate or value object, enforcing invariants, or emitting domain events.

## Persistence & data

**sqlx-persistence.md** — read when writing a repository adapter, a `query!`/`query_as!`, or reconciling an adapter record with a domain aggregate. (sqlx only — not an ORM.)

# Web Agentic — Architecture Guide

Unified documentation track for building **browser UIs around an agent SDK**. The reference
implementation is the [Pi Web](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web) application — a production Next.js
16 web app that hosts pi coding-agent sessions in the browser: browse and resume conversations,
send messages, watch tool calls stream in, configure models and skills, and inspect project files.

The docs below are written from the real Pi Web codebase (`example/` in this blueprint).
Each pattern names the exact module that implements it.

## Architecture & setup

- **architecture.md** — system diagram: Browser ↔ Next.js server ↔ in-process AgentSession
- **api-routes.md** — the full route map (sessions, agent RPC, SSE, auth, files, worktrees)
- **module-layout.md** — how `app/api`, `lib`, `components`, and `hooks` are organized
- **deployment.md** — shipping as an npx package, bin entry, ports, HTTP Basic Auth

## Session lifecycle & streaming

- **session-rpc.md** — AgentSession lifecycle: registry on `globalThis`, idle timeout, fork, startup preferences

blueprints.docs_preview:
# Documentation Index

Universal instructions for building a conforming **web-react-rust-wasm** app: a **React 19 + shadcn/ui + Storybook** thin UI over a **Rust-WASM business core**, talking to the `microservice-rust` `settings-service` backend. Each entry is imperative — read the doc when doing that task. The recurring worked example is the **tenant-scoped settings editor** (login/logout via Keycloak, shell/sidebar, reactive settings list).

The three non-negotiable references beneath all of these:

- `architecture.md` — the core↔UI↔composition-root split and the unidirectional reactive data flow (the **frontend contract**, `ui-architecture-requirements.md`, applied to React + Rust-WASM).
- `security.md` — the **frontend security contract** (`security-requirements.md` B/C/D series) as wired into this example.
- `module-layout.md` — the physical crate/layer layout the other docs assume.

## Core (the Rust-WASM boundary)

- **wasm-coreboundary.md** — read when implementing the Rust core: value types crossing, reactive streams (subscribe → snapshot → change → unsubscribe), the `#[wasm_bindgen]` JS surface, and the native-vs-wasm testability split.
- **transport-port.md** — read when implementing/calling the settings API: the swappable `SettingPort`, the REST+NDJSON wire contract, ETag/`If-Match` optimistic concurrency, and the semantic error taxonomy → `CoreError`.

## UI (React components)

- **react-components.md** — read when writing/refactoring a component: thin, prop-driven, seam-free, view-local state only, interface segregation at the boundary.
- **ui-design-system.md** — read when adding UI: shadcn/ui primitives, reuse-not-rebuild rule (B1/B2), theming, styling rules.
- **storybook.md** — read before/while writing a component: Storybook-first with injected handler doubles, headless, the correctness gate for a component.
